'''Maw-Kuen Wu''' ({{lang-zh|t=吳茂昆|p=Wú Màokūn}}; born December 6, 1949) is a Taiwanese physicist specializing in [[superconductivity]], [[cryogenics|low-temperature physics]], and [[high pressure|high-pressure physics]]. He was a professor of physics at [[University of Alabama in Huntsville]], [[Columbia University]], and [[National Tsing Hua University]], the Director of the [[Institute of Physics, Academia Sinica|Institute of Physics]] at [[Academia Sinica]], the President of [[National Dong Hwa University]], and is currently a distinguished research fellow of the Institute of Physics, [[Academia Sinica]], and international member of [[National Academy of Sciences]].
==Early life and education==
Wu was born in 1949 in [[Yuli, Hualien|Yuli Township]], [[Hualien County]], Taiwan.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maw-Kuen Wu |url=https://y105.site.nthu.edu.tw/p/406-1094-91761,r5329.php?Lang=zh-tw |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=[[National Tsing Hua University]] |language=zh}}</ref> He was the youngest of eleven children, and his mother died when he was young.<ref name="Yang1988">{{cite magazine |last=Yang |first=Meng-yu |date=1988-07-15 |title=The 90-Degree Shock: Maw-Kuen Wu's World of Superconducting Physics |url=https://www.gvm.com.tw/article/927 |magazine=[[:zh:遠見雜誌|Global Views Monthly]] |language=zh}}</ref> His family experienced financial difficulties after his father became ill and could no longer sustain his business, prompting several of Wu's older siblings to leave school and begin working.<ref name="Wu2002">{{cite news |last=Wu |first=Maw-Kuen |date=2002-06-03 |title=Deep Affection for Tamkang |url=https://tkutimes.tku.edu.tw/dtl.aspx?no=3456 |work=Tamkang Times |publisher=[[Tamkang University]] |language=zh}}</ref> He attended Yuli Elementary School, located near the [[Xiuguluan River]].<ref name="Wu2002" />

After junior high school, Wu attended [[National Hualien Senior High School|Hualien High School]] for six years.<ref name="Wu2002" /> He then enrolled at [[Tamkang University]] in 1969, studying physics.<ref>{{cite web |title=Maw-Kuen Wu |url=https://science.nchc.org.tw/science/science2007/master/09mas.htm |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=National Center for High-performance Computing |language=zh}}</ref> As an undergraduate, he also studied English and Japanese,<ref name="Wu2002" /> and developed an interest in [[superconductivity]].<ref>{{cite news |last=Kao |first=Chia-mei |date=2012-05-04 |title=National Dong Hwa University President Maw-Kuen Wu: Achieve Great Things While Young! |url=https://pr.ntnu.edu.tw/news/index.php?id=11834&mode=data |work=National Taiwan Normal University News |publisher=[[National Taiwan Normal University]] |language=zh}}</ref> He graduated with a [[Bachelor of Science]] in physics in 1973.<ref name="AcademiaSinicaWu">{{cite web |title=Maw-Kuen Wu |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?_lang=en&id=207&r=academician-n/show |access-date=2026-11-03 |website=[[Academia Sinica]]}}</ref> He then earned a [[Master of Science]] in physics from the university in 1975.<ref name="AcademiaSinicaWu" />

In 1977, Wu went to the United States to pursue graduate studies in [[solid-state physics]] at the [[University of Houston]], where he had won an academic scholarship.<ref name="Yang1988" /> He earned his [[Ph.D.]] in physics from the university in 1981.<ref name="AcademiaSinicaWu" /> That same year, he coauthored a paper examining the effects of pressure on the electrical resistance and superconducting transition temperature of barium–lead–bismuth oxide.<ref>{{cite journal |last1=Wu |first1=M. K. |last2=Meng |first2=R. L. |last3=Huang |first3=S. Z. |last4=Chu |first4=C. W. |date=1981-10-01 |title=Superconductivity in BaPb₁₋ₓBiₓO₃ near the metal-semiconductor phase boundary under pressure |url=https://doi.org/10.1103/PhysRevB.24.4075 |journal=[[Physical Review B]] |volume=24 |pages=4075–4078 |doi=10.1103/PhysRevB.24.4075}}</ref> His doctoral dissertation was titled, ''High'' ''Pressure Study on Some Unusual Magnetic and Superconducting Materials''.<ref>{{Cite web |title=https://uh.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma991003000779705701&context=L&vid=01UHO_INST:UHMAIN&lang=en&search_scope=UHMAIN_Everything&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Everything&query=any,contains,Maw-Kuen%20Wu&pfilter=rtype,exact,dissertations |url=https://uh.primo.exlibrisgroup.com/discovery/fulldisplay?docid=alma991003000779705701&context=L&vid=01UHO_INST:UHMAIN&lang=en&search_scope=UHMAIN_Everything&adaptor=Local%20Search%20Engine&tab=Everything&query=any,contains,Maw-Kuen%20Wu&pfilter=rtype,exact,dissertations |access-date=2025-04-30 |website=uh.primo.exlibrisgroup.com |language=en}}</ref>

== Career ==
Wu worked as a research scientist at his alma mater for two years, before being taken on as an [[assistant professor]] of physics at the [[University of Alabama in Huntsville]], and then subsequently promoted to [[professor]] in 1987. Along with [[Chu Ching-wu]] and  Jim Ashburn, Wu made the historic discovery of superconductivity above 77 K in [[Yttrium barium copper oxide|YBCO]] in 1987.<ref>{{cite journal
|author1=M. K. Wu |author2=J. R. Ashburn |author3=C. J. Torng |author4=P. H. Hor |author5=R. L. Meng |author6=L. Gao |author7=Z. J. Huang |author8=Y. Q. Wang |author9=C. W. Chu  |title=Superconductivity at 93 K in a new mixed-phase Y-Ba-Cu-O compound system at ambient pressure |name-list-style=amp | journal = Phys. Rev. Lett.
| volume = 58
| pages = 908–910
| year = 1987
| doi = 10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.908
| pmid = 10035069
| issue = 9
| bibcode=1987PhRvL..58..908W|doi-access=free }}</ref> According to the [[Science Citation Index]] by [[Web of Science]], Wu's 1987 work "[https://journals.aps.org/prl/abstract/10.1103/PhysRevLett.58.908 Superconductivity at 93 K in a new mixed-phase Y-Ba-Cu-O compound system at ambient pressure]" in ''[[Physical Review Letters]]'' ([[American Physical Society]]) has been cited for more than five thousand times by journal articles and is considered influential in applied science and business.<ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1987/08/16/magazine/in-the-trenches-of-science.html|title=IN THE TRENCHES OF SCIENCE|work=[[New York Times]]|date=1987-08-16}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://www.nytimes.com/1988/09/20/science/suspension-effect-astounds-scientists.html|title=Suspension Effect Astounds Scientists|work=[[New York Times]]|date=1988-09-20}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://patents.justia.com/patent/5198412|title=Method for making superconductor films|publisher=|date=1991-12-13}}</ref><ref>{{cite web|url=https://journals.aps.org/prl/heating-up-of-superconductors|title=Heating up of Superconductors|publisher=[[Physical Review Letters]]|date=2017}}</ref>
Wu was then invited to teach at the [[National Tsing Hua University]], and conduct further research in [[high-temperature superconductivity]].

Maw-Kuen Wu first entered the cabinet; served as [[National Science Council|minister of the National Science Council]] from 2004 to 2006. In 2018, he was named as the [[Ministry of Education (Taiwan)|minister of the Ministry of Education]] and resigned after 41 days.<ref>{{cite news|title=Education minister's resignation approved: Cabinet spokesman|url=http://focustaiwan.tw/news/aipl/201805290018.aspx|accessdate=29 May 2018|agency=Central News Agency|date=29 May 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|title=Taiwan Cabinet confirms approval of new education minister's resignation|url=https://www.taiwannews.com.tw/en/news/3442755|accessdate=29 May 2018|work=Taiwan News|date=29 May 2018}}</ref> Wu was subsequently impeached by the [[Control Yuan]], which charged him with violating the Public Functionary Service Act and the Act on the Recusal of Public Servants Due to Conflict of Interest.<ref>{{cite news |last1=Tu |first1=Aaron |last2=Chien |first2=Huei-ru |title=Control Yuan impeaches Wu Maw-kuen |url=http://www.taipeitimes.com/News/taiwan/archives/2018/07/04/2003696049 |accessdate=4 July 2018 |work=Taipei Times |date=4 July 2018}}</ref>

==Personal life==
Maw-Kuen Wu and his wife have two children.{{Citation needed|date=April 2025}}

==Academic honors==
* 1988 USA Chinese Association of Engineering Annual Award
* 1988 [[State of Alabama]] Resolution
* 1988 [[University of Alabama]] Research Award
* 1988 U.S.A. [[National Academy of Sciences]] Comstock Prize
* 1989 Tamkang Golden Eagle Award
* 1994 Fellow, [[Chinese Physical Society]]
* 1994 [[Bernd T. Matthias Prize]]
* 1995 Y. T. Lee Outstanding Scientist Award
* 1998 [[NASA]] Special Awards
* 1998 Member, [[Academia Sinica]]<ref>{{cite news |title=Maw-Kuen Wu |url=https://academicians.sinica.edu.tw/index.php?r=academician-n%2Fshow&id=207 |access-date=10 September 2023 |publisher=Academia Sinica}}</ref>
* 2007 Ettore Majorana-Erice-Science for Peace Prize
* 2009 Taiwanese-American Foundation (TAF) Award
* 2010-03 Germany [[Humboldt Research Award]]
